reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures, such as Fig. 1, which shows the time-domain waveform of the LFM signal before and after transmission, and the amplitude-frequency response of the LFM probe within the ISAC system. Fig. 2 depicts the experimental setup, while Fig. 3 shows the Rayleigh scattering traces of the LFM probe and pre-distorted probe, as well as the phase waterfall, phase variance, and PSD curves of the vibration with LFM probe and pre-distorted probe.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The system uses a digital subcarrier multiplexing (DSCM)-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the sensing probe is pre-compensated using the frequency response data from the forward communication link. The ISAC system consists of a narrow linewidth laser, an arbitrary waveform generator, and a coherent receiver. The sensing component comprises a continuous linear frequency-modulated (LFM) probe, while the communication payload consists of two 30 GBaud 16QAM DSCM signals.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports a spatial resolution of 1 m in a 40-km fiber link, with an SNR improvement of 2.4 dB in distributed sensing. The experimental results show that the pre-compensation enabled by forward communication information results in significant improvements in both SNR and spatial resolution. The reported metrics are physically consistent with the system description and experimental setup.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper solves the problem of frequency-dependent distortions in LFM probes used in distributed fiber optic sensing systems. The proposed ISAC system with pre-compensation enables simultaneous sensing and communication over a 40-km fiber link with minimal impact on both performances. However, the paper does not address the potential challenges of scaling up the system to longer distances or more complex network topologies.
